title: CSS Grid: rows, columns, areas and the implicit grid

videos.script: Flexbox lays things out along one line. That is enough for a menu, a row of buttons, a picture beside its text. {{line}} A page is not a line. It has a header across the top, a column of content, a sidebar, a footer. A gallery of book covers has rows and columns that should line up. {{grid}} CSS Grid is the layout system built for that. You draw the columns and the rows on the container. Then you place the items into the grid you drew. {{fr}} It brings a new unit, the fraction, written fr. One fr is one share of the space that is left. You will measure it, and it does the arithmetic Flexbox made you think about. {{areas}} It also lets you name parts of the layout, and write the whole page as a little picture in text. Header across the top. Navigation beside the main content. Footer across the bottom. {{fit}} And it can decide by itself how many columns fit. The same rule gives four columns on a wide screen and one on a phone, without a media query. {{order}} Grid is powerful enough to put any item anywhere, and that power has a cost for anybody reading the page in order. {{end}} The lesson ends by building the bookshop's home page from it. {{close}}
